correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the source characteristic equation. At zero advection the mixed Neumann--Dirichlet eigenvalues are explicit, reducing the (1,1) versus (2,0) branch intersection to one scalar function G. Exact endpoint inequalities give opposite signs, an explicit derivative bound proves G is strictly decreasing, and the resulting root lies where exactly modes 1 and 2 satisfy the imaginary-root condition. Simplicity follows directly from the characteristic derivative. The gauge-transformed spatial eigenproblem has simple roots, so the implicit-function theorem continues the transverse intersection to sufficiently small positive advection. The included checker only reproduces the representative numerical point and characteristic residuals; no numerical experiment is used as the existence proof.

value.rationale: The claim changes a central codimension-two conclusion of the motivating paper. It identifies an omitted interaction between spatial mode number and Hopf branch index, proves that the omitted intersections persist for genuinely positive advection, and isolates a natural four-dimensional local bifurcation problem. This is not a parameter-table recomputation or a tiny numerical shift.
